subject.title: Codex app-server approval-policy promotion from `before_tool_call` hooks is fleet-wide; make it scope-aware

question: Should OpenClaw make hook jurisdiction a declarative plugin API and use it to narrow Codex app-server approval promotion, while retaining global promotion for legacy unscoped hooks?
rationale: The current global promotion is a deliberate safety boundary; maintainers must choose the durable plugin-contract semantics before a scoped matcher can safely govern native Codex tool approval.

options.title: Add declarative scoped hooks
options.body: Add agent/session scope metadata to the plugin hook API, use it in per-run promotion, and preserve global behavior when metadata is omitted.

options.title: Keep global fail-closed behavior
options.body: Retain fleet-wide promotion and document that any registered pre-tool hook affects all Codex app-server runs.

options.title: Design an operator policy layer first
options.body: Defer hook API changes and decide whether a separate per-agent Codex approval-policy control better matches the product boundary.

recommendation.title: Add declarative scoped hooks
recommendation.body: Add agent/session scope metadata to the plugin hook API, use it in per-run promotion, and preserve global behavior when metadata is omitted.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant global hook-runner behavior traces to the original hook-wiring work, making this the strongest available owner signal for the API boundary.
